Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
236 PM EDT Thu Oct 8 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

Increasing confidence in tidal flooding later this weekend due 
to increased southerly flow combined with high astronomical 
tides. See the Coastal Flooding section below for more 
information. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Sunny & mild conditions continue through the end of the
  week. 

- 2) Remnants of Hurricane Isaias to arrive Saturday night.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Sunny & mild conditions continue through the end
of the week. 

Current surface analysis depicts that the cold front has largely 
pushed through the region this morning. In its wake, dry air builds 
in from the west as high pressure moves in overhead. A few wind 
gusts could reach around 20 knots late this afternoon before 
diminishing overnight as the front fully transitions out of the 
region. Temperatures remain in the mid-to-upper 70s today & tomorrow 
as upper-level ridging briefly builds over the Appalachians, with 
dewpoints ranging generally in the 30s across most areas. As most of 
CONUS remains quiet off to our west, clear skies and light winds 
should continue to dominate over the next 36-48 hours ahead of any 
potential remnants of Hurricane Isaias. 


KEY MESSAGE 2... Remnants of Hurricane Isaias to arrive Saturday
night.


Latest guidance show rain associated with remnants of Isaias 
arriving in central VA Saturday evening, a little quicker than what 
it was shown yesterday, and spreading northeast across the rest of 
the fcst area late Saturday night, reaching the Susquehanna River by 
12Z Sunday. The rain will be moderately intense during the overnight 
hours Sat night through Sunday morning, and begin to diminish in 
intensity mid afternoon Sunday as mid-level dry slot begins to move 
in from the southwest. Ensemble guidance shows generally one to two 
inches of rain falling, with the heaviest/most intense rainfall 
falling in a roughly 12-hr period from 06Z-18Z Sun. Given the long 
duration and stratiform type, no flooding is expected. As for the 
risk of severe wx, if it were to occur, it would be Sunday night, 
with the greatest risk south of Point Lookout into the VA Tidewater 
region. Some showers could linger into Monday morning as the mid-
level circulation crosses the area. 

A strong cold front associated with a deepening northern stream 
trough is then fcst to cross the area Tue night bringing autumn 
chill for the middle and second half of next week. 


&&

.AVIATION /18Z THURSDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...

In the immediate wake of the cold front, clear & dry conditions are 
expected to persist over the region over the next 36-48 hours.
Prevailing VFR conditions are anticipated across all terminals in 
the near term as high pressure builds overhead. KCHO could see a bit 
more cloud cover between Friday and Saturday as tropical remnants 
from Hurricane Isaias begin to push north, but VFR conditions are 
still expected to prevail through Saturday morning. 

Breezier winds from this afternoon will diminish overnight, flowing 
out of the W to WNW. Winds could begin to shift more northeasterly 
on Saturday. 

Rain is expected Saturday night through mid-afternoon Sunday, 
becoming lighter and more showery Sunday evening. A thunderstorm 
can't be ruled out Sunday night. Winds should strengthen Saturday 
night into Sunday as pressure gradient tightens. Wouldn't rule out 
some LLWS if a strong inversion develops. Showers should end by 
midday Monday. Expect IFR conditions late Sunday night through 
Sunday night with conditions improving Monday. 

&&

.MARINE...

Winds diminish below SCA criteria over the Chesapeake Bay later 
tonight. Light northwesterly winds shift easterly on Saturday, 
becoming gustier by Sunday as tropical remnants from Hurricane 
Isaias begin to track east over the Mid-Atlantic. Additional SCAs 
remain a likelihood at this point until any remaining tropical 
remnants move through. 

SCA conditions are likely starting Saturday night and continuing 
through Sunday. Another period of SCA conditions is likely Tue night 
into Wed with gales possible. 


&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...

Minor coastal flooding seems likely at sensitive locations Sunday 
evening due to rising water levels due to strengthening SE or S 
winds combined with high astronomical tides due to a New Moon. 
Until then, tide levels remain below action stage.


&&
